newsitem.title: FRANCE: French have good memories of Mitterrand.
newsitem.headline: French have good memories of Mitterrand.

text.p: A majority of French people have good memories of the 14-year rule of Socialist president Francois Mittterand, a year after he died, an opinion poll said on Thursday.

The Sofres poll, to be published in pro-government Le Figaro Magazine newspaper on Saturday, said 53 percent believed Mitterrand's actions in power from 1981 to 1995 had been positive and 65 percent had good memories of him.
Mitterrand, 77, died of cancer last January 8, seven months after serving out his second seven-year term.
He was most remembered for social reforms -- cutting the working week to 39 hours, bringing the retirement age forward to 60 from 65 and establishing state benefits for the destitute.

Next came the abolition of the death penalty and guillotine, the Maastricht treaty on European union and major construction works to build the Louvre museum glass pyramid, a giant library and the Bastille Opera house.

The 1,000 voters questioned in the poll ranked Mitterrand's main characteristics as being faithful to his ideas, power-hungry, bent on social progress, megalomaniac, opportunistic, visionnary, honest and devoid of principles.
An overwhelming 82 percent said they were not shocked to learn that he had a grown-up illegitimate daughter.
